page: Microsoft Azure M176-88bds_v3 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for enterprise workloads requiring extensive RAM capacity and high compute density. The server is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8473C processors operating at up to 4.0 GHz, configured with 44 physical cores and 88 virtual CPUs. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache pool. Instruction set support encompasses AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8). Acceleration hardware is not included, with 0 GPUs provisioned. Local storage is supplied via a 429 GB SSD, complementing the instance's block storage performance.

System memory totals 1536.0 GB, providing an allocation of 17.45 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded performance, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 20,824.0, PassMark CPU scoring 94,297.76, and PassMark database operations logging 34,867.58. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high uncached throughput, registering 419.99 GB/sec read and 186.04 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. Key-value transactional capacity is substantial, with Redis achieving 109.3 million SET operations per second, while static web serving demonstrates throughput of 102.17 GB/sec. CPU-driven LLM inference reaches 241.98 tokens/sec on prompt processing for 7B models and 35.03 tokens/sec on 70B models.

Cost efficiency is centered on high memory density and dedicated core allocation. Rather than maximizing single-thread performance, which scores within the average range in stress-ng tests (2058.29), value is derived from concurrent parallel execution across 88 vCPUs coupled with over 1.5 TB of memory. The local 429 GB SSD serves primarily as scratch space or caching rather than bulk persistent capacity, requiring external block storage for large disk footprints.

The hardware profile aligns with large in-memory databases (such as SAP HANA or high-volume Redis clusters), enterprise relational database systems, large-scale data analytics, and memory-bound transactional applications that demand extreme memory overhead and robust parallel computing capacity.
